title: The Only 3-Ingredient Banana Pancakes That Don't Turn Into Mush
description: Skip the sugar and the mountain of dirty dishes. These 3-ingredient banana pancakes are fast, healthy, and actually flip without falling apart in the pan.
story: Look, I live in a third-floor walk-up with a kitchen the size of a closet. If a recipe requires more than one bowl and a skillet, I’m probably not making it after a long shift. I had these two sad, spotted bananas from Trader Joe's staring me down, and I wasn't about to bake a whole loaf of bread. The first time I tested this, I tried the 'just egg and banana' version I saw on TikTok. Total disaster. It was basically a sweet, soggy omelet that stuck to everything. I learned the hard way: you need a handful of oats to give these guys some actual backbone. Now, this is my go-to when I want something sweet but don't want to deal with a sugar crash or a sink full of flour-coated whisks. It's fast, cheap, and I can eat them straight off the spatula if I'm feeling particularly lazy.
ingredients: 2 medium very ripe bananas (the more spots, the better)
1/2 cup Quaker quick oats (blitzed or left whole for texture)
1 teaspoon avocado oil or Kerrygold butter for the pan
A pinch of kosher salt to balance the sweetness
instructions: Step 1: Use a fork to mash the bananas in a medium bowl until they look like a thick liquid. Don't leave big chunks or the pancakes will break.
Step 2: Crack in the eggs and add the oats, cinnamon, and salt. Whisk it vigorously with the same fork until the batter is consistent and slightly bubbly.
Step 3: Heat your skillet over medium-low heat with a tiny bit of butter. Drop about 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake. Small pancakes are way easier to flip than giant ones.
Step 4: Wait until you see tiny bubbles on the surface and the edges look set, about 3 minutes. Flip carefully and cook for another 2 minutes until golden brown.
proHack: Do not rush the flip. These don't have gluten to hold them together, so if you try to flip them while the middle is still wet, you'll end up with a banana scramble. Wait for those edges to look matte and firm.
storage: Store leftovers in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days. To reheat, just pop them in the toaster on a low setting—it crisps the edges back up perfectly.

faqs.question: Can I make these without oats?
faqs.answer: You can, but they will be very soft and hard to flip. If you're grain-free, swap the oats for 2 tablespoons of almond flour or coconut flour instead.

faqs.question: How do I keep them from sticking to the pan?
faqs.answer: Make sure your pan is actually non-stick and don't skimp on a little bit of fat like avocado oil or butter. Keep the heat at medium-low; high heat burns the natural sugars in the banana before the egg sets.
